essay.en:
The surah opens with glorification. God declares Himself beyond every partner and, in that spirit of praise, points to the night journey of His servant: He carried the Prophet by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose environs He has blessed, that He might show him some of His signs [1]. Commentators identify the Farthest Mosque as Bayt al-Maqdis in Jerusalem, called the farthest for its distance from the Sacred Mosque at Mecca [4]. According to al-Tusi and most exegetes, the Prophet was taken up that same night to the seventh heaven and the Lote-tree, shown wonders that deepened his certainty, and this happened while he was awake, not in a dream [7].

From the journey the passage turns to Moses, given the Book as a guide for the Children of Israel and told to take no trustee besides God, they being the descendants of those carried in the ark with Noah, a grateful servant. Tabatabai reads the seven verses that follow as a prelude, set between the first verse and the ninth, illustrating God's constant practice with the nations [2]. God decreed to the Children of Israel that they would twice corrupt the land; when the first came, He raised against them servants of great might who ransacked their homes, then their turn returned. Good and evil, the passage insists, fall back upon the souls that do them. When the second warning came, their faces were made wretched and the Temple entered as before. Mercy is still held out, but reversion brings reversion, and hell is made a prison for the faithless [5].

The passage closes by returning to this community: this Quran guides to what is most upright [3], giving the believers who act righteously the good news of a great reward [6], while those who deny the Hereafter are promised a painful punishment.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: جاء جبرائيل وميكائيل وإسرافيل بالبراق إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله فأخذ واحد باللجام وواحد بالركاب وسوى الآخر عليه ثيابه فتضعضعت البراق فلطمها جبرائيل ثم قال لها اسكني يا براق فما ركبك نبي قبله ولا يركبك بعده مثله … ومعه جبرائيل يريه الآيات من السماء والأرض
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Jibril, Mikail and Israfil brought the Buraq to the Messenger of God. One took its bridle, one its stirrup, the third settled his garments upon him. When the Buraq shied, Jibril struck it: Be still; no prophet before him has ridden you. Then Jibril went on showing him the signs of heaven and earth.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: فنظر إلى السّماءِ مرّة وإلى الكعبة مرّة ثم قال سبحان الذي أسرى بعبده ليلاً من المسجد الحرام إلى المسجد الأقصى … ليس كما يقولون ولكنّه أسرى به من هذه إلى هذه وأشار بيده إلى السّماءِ وقال ما بينهما حرم

text.en: He looked once at the sky and once at the Kaaba, then recited this verse. The people of Iraq say the Prophet was carried to Bayt al-Maqdis. It is not as they say: he was carried from this to this - and he pointed to the sky - and what lies between them is sanctuary.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: كان نوح إذا أمسى وأصبح يقول أمسيت أشهد أنه ما أمسى بي من نعمة في دين أو دنيا فإنها من الله وحده لا شريك له له الحمد علي بها كثيراً والشكر كثيراً فأنزل الله أنه كان عبداً شكوراً فهذا كان شكره
narrations.chain: His father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shamir, from Jabir, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Noah, morning and evening, would say: I bear witness that no blessing of religion or world reaches me but from God alone, who has no partner; to Him abundant praise and thanks for it. So God revealed that he was a grateful servant; this was his thankfulness.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لَتُفْسِدُنَّ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَّتَيْنِ قَالَ قَتْلُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ (عليه السلام) وَ طَعْنُ الْحَسَنِ (عليه السلام) وَ لَتَعْلُنَّ عُلُوًّا كَبِيراً قَالَ قَتْلُ الْحُسَيْنِ (عليه السلام) … بَعَثْنا عَلَيْكُمْ عِباداً لَنا أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ فَجاسُوا خِلالَ الدِّيارِ قَوْمٌ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ قَبْلَ خُرُوجِ الْقَائِمِ (عليه السلام) فَلَا يَدَعُونَ وَتْراً لآِلِ مُحَمَّدٍ إِلَّا قَتَلُوهُ
narrations.chain: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Batal, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: 'You will cause corruption twice' is the killing of Ali ibn Abi Talib and the stabbing of al-Hasan; 'you will perpetrate great tyranny' is the killing of al-Husayn. The servants of great might are a people God raises before the Qaim's rising, who leave no enemy of Muhammad's family unslain.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: قَالَ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ فِي قَوْلِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ إِنْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ لانْفُسِكُمْ وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَها قَالَ إِنْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ لانْفُسِكُمْ وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَهَا رَبٌّ يَغْفِرُ لَهَا
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan, Muhammad ibn Bakran al-Naqqash and Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed al-Hamadani, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from his father

text.en: Concerning 'If you do good, you do good to your own souls, and if you do evil, it is for them,' he said: and if you do evil, it has a Lord who forgives it.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: في الكافي عن الصادق عليه السلام أي يدعو وعنه عليه السلام يهدي إلى الإمام عليه السلام

text.en: Asked about 'this Quran guides to what is most upright,' he said it means it invites; and, in another report, that it guides to the Imam.

perspectives.en: On the two corruptions of the Children of Israel (verses 4 to 8) the readings diverge. Sunni exegetes take the words historically: al-Tabari relates that the first corruption was the killing of Zakariyya, after which God sent a foreign king against them to overrun their land [33]. The Shia narrations read the same verses as a pattern for this community: al-Kulayni records from Imam al-Sadiq that the first corruption is the killing of Ali and the stabbing of al-Hasan, and the great tyranny the killing of al-Husayn, with the reckoning coming through a force God raises before the rising of the Qaim [58].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وقد افتتحت السورة فيما ترومه من التسبيح بالإِشارة إلى معراج النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فذكر اسراؤه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من المسجد الحرام إلى المسجد الأقصى وهو بيت المقدس

sources.gloss: The surah opens, in the glorification it intends, by pointing to the Prophet's ascension, mentioning his night journey from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, which is Bayt al-Maqdis.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: ومن ذلك يستنتج أن الآيات السبع كالتوطئة لما سيذكر بعدها من جريان هذه السنة العامة في هذه الأُمة، والآيات السبع كالمعترضة بين الآية الأولى والتاسعة.

sources.gloss: From this it follows that the seven verses are a prelude to the running of this general divine practice in this community, and the seven verses stand interposed between the first verse and the ninth.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: إن هذا القرآن يهدي للتي هي أقوم } أي للملة التي هي أقوم

sources.gloss: 'Indeed this Quran guides to what is most upright' means to the creed that is most upright.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: إلى المسجد الأقصى } يعني بيت المقدس وإنما قال الأقصى لبعد المسافة بينه وبين المسجد الحرام

sources.gloss: 'To the Farthest Mosque' means Bayt al-Maqdis; it is called the farthest because of the distance between it and the Sacred Mosque.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وأراد بالفساد الظلم وأخذ المال وقتل الأنبياء وسفك الدماء

sources.gloss: By 'corruption' is meant injustice, seizing wealth, killing the prophets, and shedding blood.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ويبشر المؤمنين الذين يعملون الصالحات أن لهم } أي بأن لهم { أجراً كبيراً } أي ثواباً عظيماً على طاعاتهم

sources.gloss: It gives the believers who do righteous deeds good news that they have a great reward, meaning a great recompense for their obedience.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وعند أصحابنا وأكثر أصحاب التأويل، وذكره الجبائي ايضاً: انه عرج به في تلك الليلة الى السماء وأت حتى بلغ سدرة المنتهى في السماء السابعة، واراه الله من آيات السموات والارض ما ازداد به معرفة ويقيناً، وكان ذلك في يقظته دون منامه

sources.gloss: According to our companions and most exegetes, he was taken up that night to heaven, reaching the Lote-tree in the seventh heaven, and God showed him signs of the heavens and the earth that increased his certainty; this was while he was awake, not in sleep.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: جاء جبرائيل وميكائيل وإسرافيل بالبراق إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله

sources.gloss: Jibril, Mikail and Israfil brought the Buraq to the Messenger of God.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: كان نوح إذا أمسى وأصبح يقول أمسيت أشهد أنه ما أمسى بي من نعمة في دين أو دنيا فإنها من الله وحده لا شريك له له الحمد علي بها كثيراً والشكر كثيراً فأنزل الله أنه كان عبداً شكوراً فهذا كان شكره

sources.gloss: Noah, morning and evening, would say: I bear witness that no blessing of religion or world reaches me but from God alone, who has no partner; to Him much praise and thanks for it. So God revealed that he was a grateful servant; this was his thankfulness.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: ليس كما يقولون ولكنّه أسرى به من هذه إلى هذه وأشار بيده إلى السّماءِ وقال ما بينهما حرم

sources.gloss: It is not as they say; rather he was carried from this to this - and he pointed to the sky - and said: what lies between them is sanctuary.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وعنه عليه السلام يهدي إلى الإمام عليه السلام

sources.gloss: And from him (al-Sadiq): it guides to the Imam.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: فكان أوّل الفسادين: قتل زكريا، فبعث الله علـيهم ملك النبط

sources.gloss: The first of the two corruptions was the killing of Zakariyya, so God sent against them the king of the Nabat.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: لَتُفْسِدُنَّ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَّتَيْنِ قَالَ قَتْلُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ (عليه السلام) وَ طَعْنُ الْحَسَنِ (عليه السلام)

sources.gloss: 'You will cause corruption in the land twice' - he said: the killing of Ali ibn Abi Talib and the stabbing of al-Hasan.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: قَالَ إِنْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ لانْفُسِكُمْ وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَهَا رَبٌّ يَغْفِرُ لَهَا

sources.gloss: He said: 'If you do good, you do good for your own souls, and if you do evil, it is for them' - a Lord who forgives it.

essay.en: This is the second passage of Surah al-Israa, continuing its account of how the Quran guides people and how God rewards or punishes their response [1]. It opens by reproaching man: in his haste he prays for what harms him as readily as for what benefits him, unable to tell the two apart [1]. Tabatabai takes 'man' here as the whole human race and 'prayer' as any seeking, whether voiced or pursued through action [1]. God then points to the night and the day as two signs. Al-Tabrisi notes that each carries its own benefit, earning by day and rest by night, and that the day was made lightsome so that people may seek their livelihood and reckon the years and the count of time [2]. The passage turns to accountability. Every person's deeds are fastened to his neck, never leaving him, and on the Day of Resurrection they are produced as an open book he is told to read against himself. Tabatabai holds that the omen and the book are one thing: a person's own deeds [1]. God then lays down a principle. Whoever is guided is guided for himself, whoever strays strays against himself, no soul bears another's burden, and He does not destroy a community until He has sent it a messenger [1]. Next comes the pattern of ruin: when God wills to destroy a town its affluent transgress, the word falls due, and it is destroyed; the commentators divide over what His command to them means [1]. Many generations have perished since Noah. The passage then weighs two desires: whoever wants the fleeting world is given a measure of it and then hell, while the believer who strives for the Hereafter has his striving appreciated. God extends His unrestricted bounty to both, yet the ranks of the Hereafter are far greater [1]. It closes by forbidding the worship of any god besides Allah, which al-Mizan reads as the conclusion the whole passage has been driving toward [1].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لما خلق الله آدم و نفخ فيه من روحه، وثب ليقوم قبل أن يتم خلقه فسقط، فقال الله عز و جل: وكان الإنسان عجولاً
narrations.chain: From Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When God created Adam and breathed His spirit into him, he leapt up to stand before his creation was complete, and so he fell. God then said: 'And man was ever hasty.'

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: أخبرني عن هذا السواد في القمر؟ … هو قول الله: { فَمَحَوْنَآ آيَةَ ٱلَّيلِ }
narrations.chain: From Abu al-Tufayl

text.en: Ibn al-Kawwa asked: 'Tell me about this blackness in the moon.' He said: 'It is God's word: Then We faded out the sign of the night.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: خيره و شره معه حيث كان، لا يستطيع فراقه، حتى يعطى كتابه يوم القيامة بما عمل
narrations.chain: In the report of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: His good and his evil are with him wherever he is; he cannot part from them until he is given his book on the Day of Resurrection with what he did.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يذكر العبد جميع ما عمل و ما كتب عليه، حتى كأنه فعله تلك الساعة
narrations.chain: From Khalid ibn Najih, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The servant recalls everything he did and everything written against him, as though he had done it that very hour.

note.en: Al-Mizan reads the withheld punishment as worldly destruction, sent only after a warning messenger, and takes 'no soul bears another's burden' to mean each answers for his own deeds alone [1].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: أمرنا مترفيها مشددة منصوبة، تفسيرها: كثرنا، و قال: لا قرأتها مخففة
narrations.chain: From Hamran, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: 'We command its affluent ones,' read with the doubled letter: its meaning is 'We multiplied them.' And he said: I do not recite it in the light form.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: هو مخاطبة للنبي و المعنى للناس … إن الله بعث نبيه بإياك أعني و اسمعي يا جارة

text.en: The address is to the Prophet, but the meaning is for the people: God sent His Prophet with the proverb, 'I mean you, but listen, O neighbour.'

perspectives.en: Verse 15 says no soul bears another's burden. Al-Tabrisi draws from it a clear proof that the children of unbelievers are not punished with their parents in the Fire [3], and al-Tusi reads it against the Mujbira, since God has made clear that no one is seized for another's crime [6]. Ibn Kathir, on the same verse, does not settle the fate of those who die as children or before a messenger reaches them: he gathers conflicting reports, recording both the view that such children are with their parents in the Fire and the view that they are tested on the Day of Resurrection [42].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: لكن جنس الإِنسان عجول لا يفرق لعجلته بين الخير والشر بل يطلب كل ما لاح له

sources.gloss: But the human race is hasty; in its haste it does not distinguish good from evil, and seeks whatever appears to it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وجعلنا الليل والنهار آيتين أي دلالتين يدلاّن على وحدانية خالقهما لما في كل واحد منهما من الفوائد من الكسب بالنهار والاستراحة بالليل

sources.gloss: 'We made the night and day two signs,' that is, two indications of their Creator's oneness, for in each is a benefit: earning by day and rest by night.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وفي هذا دلالة واضحة على بطلان قول من يقول إن أطفال الكفار يعذّبون مع آبائهم في النار

sources.gloss: In this is clear proof of the falsity of the claim that the children of unbelievers are punished with their fathers in the Fire.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفي الآية دلالة على بطلان قول المجبرة: من ان الله يعذب اطفال الكفار بكفر آبائهم، لانه بين أَنه لا يأخذ احداً بجرم غيره

sources.gloss: In the verse is proof of the falsity of the Mujbira's claim that God punishes the children of unbelievers for their fathers' disbelief, for He has made clear that He seizes no one for another's crime.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لما خلق الله آدم و نفخ فيه من روحه، وثب ليقوم قبل أن يتم خلقه فسقط، فقال الله عز و جل: وكان الإنسان عجولاً

sources.gloss: When God created Adam and breathed His spirit into him, he leapt up to stand before his creation was complete and fell; so God said, 'And man was ever hasty.'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هو قول الله: { فَمَحَوْنَآ آيَةَ ٱلَّيلِ }

sources.gloss: It is God's word: Then We faded out the sign of the night.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: خيره و شره معه حيث كان، لا يستطيع فراقه، حتى يعطى كتابه يوم القيامة بما عمل

sources.gloss: His good and his evil are with him wherever he is; he cannot part from them until he is given his book on the Day of Resurrection with what he did.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أمرنا مترفيها مشددة منصوبة، تفسيرها: كثرنا، و قال: لا قرأتها مخففة

sources.gloss: 'We command its affluent ones,' with the doubled letter: its meaning is 'We multiplied them'; and he said, 'I do not recite it in the light form.'

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: ومنهم من جزم لهم بالنار لقوله عليه السلام هم مع آبائهم، ومنهم من ذهب إلى أنهم يمتحنون يوم القيامة في العرصات

sources.gloss: Some are certain they go to the Fire, citing his saying 'they are with their fathers,' and some hold that they are tested on the Day of Resurrection in the plains of gathering.

essay.en:
Al-Mizan reads these eight verses as a set of the universals of the religion, placed right after the promise that this Quran guides to that which is most upright [1]. The list opens at its summit: worship God alone. Majma al-Bayan and al-Tibyan note that 'your Lord has decreed' here carries the sense of a binding command, not a decree that compels, which is the reading of Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan and Qatada [4].

Joined to that first duty is kindness to parents. The verse turns to the hardest moment, when one or both of them reach old age at your side: do not say 'Fie' to them, do not chide them, speak to them noble words, and lower to them the wing of humility. Majma al-Bayan explains that old age is singled out because that is when a parent's need for care is greatest [2]. The child is then taught a prayer: 'My Lord! Have mercy on them, just as they reared me when I was small.'

Verse 25 turns inward, since your Lord knows best what is in your hearts, and it promises forgiveness to the penitent. al-Tibyan glosses the penitent, the awwab, as the one who keeps turning back to God [5].

The passage moves next to wealth. Give the relatives their due, and the needy and the traveller, but do not squander. Here the Shia commentators read the relatives as the Prophet's own kin, and report that the verse gave Fatimah Fadak [3]. Squandering is condemned sharply: the wasteful are brothers of satans, and Satan is ungrateful to his Lord. And if you must hold back, still hoping for the provision you await from your Lord, speak to them gentle words.

The passage closes on a balance: keep your hand neither chained to your neck nor flung wide open, or you will sit blameworthy and regretful. The reason follows at once, for it is your Lord who widens and narrows provision, and He is well aware of His servants.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الإحسان: أن تحسن صحبتهما، و لا تكلفهما أن يسألاك شيئا مما يحتاجان إليه، و إن كانا مستغنيين
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Walad al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Kindness is that you keep them good company, and that you do not make them ask you for anything they need, even if they are well off.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أدنى العقوق أف، و لو علم الله عز و جل شيئا أهون منه لنهى عنه
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hadid ibn Hakim, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The least of disobedience to parents is 'Fie'; had God known of anything slighter than it, He would have forbidden that.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الأواب: التواب المتعبد، الراجع عن ذنبه

text.en: The penitent (awwab) is the one who repents, devotes himself to worship, and turns back from his sin.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لما أنزل الله تعالى { وَآتِ ذَا ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ حَقَّهُ وَٱلْمِسْكِينَ } قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله): يا جبرئيل، قد عرفت المسكين، فمن ذو القربى؟ قال: هم أقاربك، فدعا حسنا و حسينا و فاطمة
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When 'Give the relatives their due, and the needy' came down, the Messenger of God said, 'Gabriel, I know the needy; who are the relatives?' He said, 'They are your kin.' So he called Hasan, Husayn and Fatimah.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: من أنفق شيئا في غير طاعة الله فهو مبذر، و من أنفق في سبيل الخير فهو مقتصد
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Whoever spends anything in other than obedience to God is a squanderer, and whoever spends in the way of good is moderate.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) كان لا يسأله أحد من الدنيا شيئا إلا أعطاه … فأخذ قميصه فرمى به إليه، فأدبه الله تبارك و تعالى على القصد فقال: { وَلاَ تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلَىٰ عُنُقِكَ وَلاَ تَبْسُطْهَا كُلَّ ٱلْبَسْطِ فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُوماً مَّحْسُوراً }
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Ijlan

text.en: No one ever asked the Messenger of God for anything of this world without his giving it. A woman sent her son to ask for his very shirt, and he took it off and threw it to him. So God trained him to moderation, revealing, 'Do not keep your hand chained to your neck...'

perspectives.en: The commentators divide over the relatives. The Shia works read them as the Prophet's own kin: Majma al-Bayan reports that when the verse came down the Prophet gave Fatimah Fadak [3]. al-Tabari prefers the general sense, one's own blood relations whom God enjoins you to keep close [23]. Ibn Kathir goes further and rejects the Fatimah and Fadak report outright, holding it unsound because this sura is Meccan while Fadak was taken only in year seven, so he judges the report a fabrication [30].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: عدة من كليات الدين يذكرها الله سبحانه وهي تتبع قوله قبل آيات { إن هذا القرآن يهدي للتي هي أقوم } الآية.

sources.gloss: A number of the universals of the religion, which God mentions following His earlier words, 'Indeed this Quran guides to that which is most upright.'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وخصَّ حال الكبر وإن كان من الواجب طاعة الوالدين على كل حال لأن الحاجة أكثر في تلك الحال إلى التعهد والخدمة

sources.gloss: He singled out old age, though obeying parents is a duty in every state, because the need for care and service is greater then.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: لما نزل قولـه وآت ذا القربى حقه أعطى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فاطمة فدكاً.

sources.gloss: From Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: when 'Give the relatives their due' came down, the Messenger of God gave Fatimah Fadak.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: معنى قوله { وقضى ربك أَلا تعبدوا إِلاّ إِياه } أمر، في قول ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة وابن زيد.

sources.gloss: 'And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him' means He commanded, according to Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatada and Ibn Zayd.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: معنى { الأوّابين } التوابين وهم الذين يتوبون مرة بعد مرة

sources.gloss: The 'penitents' (awwabin) means those who repent, turning back time after time.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الإحسان: أن تحسن صحبتهما، و لا تكلفهما أن يسألاك شيئا مما يحتاجان إليه، و إن كانا مستغنيين

sources.gloss: Kindness is to keep them good company and not to make them ask you for what they need, even if they are well off.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الأواب: التواب المتعبد، الراجع عن ذنبه

sources.gloss: The penitent (awwab) is the one who repents, devotes himself to worship, and returns from his sin.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: من أنفق شيئا في غير طاعة الله فهو مبذر، و من أنفق في سبيل الخير فهو مقتصد

sources.gloss: Whoever spends anything in other than obedience to God is a squanderer; whoever spends in the way of good is moderate.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فأدبه الله تبارك و تعالى على القصد فقال: { وَلاَ تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلَىٰ عُنُقِكَ وَلاَ تَبْسُطْهَا كُلَّ ٱلْبَسْطِ فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُوماً مَّحْسُوراً }

sources.gloss: So God trained him to moderation, revealing, 'Do not keep your hand chained to your neck, nor open it altogether, or you will sit blameworthy and regretful.'

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: وأولـى التأويـلـين عندي بـالصواب، تأويـل من تأوّل ذلك أنها بـمعنى وصية الله عبـاده بصلة قرابـات أنفسهم وأرحامهم

sources.gloss: The sounder of the two readings to me is that it means God's charge to His servants to keep the ties of their own kin and relatives.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: وهذا الحديث مشكل لو صح إسناده لأن الآية مكية، وفدك إنما فتحت مع خيبر سنة سبع من الهجرة … فهو إذاً حديث منكر، والأشبه أنه من وضع الرافضة

sources.gloss: This report is problematic even if its chain were sound, for the verse is Meccan while Fadak was only taken with Khaybar in year seven; so it is a denounced report, most likely a fabrication.

essay.en:
These ten verses gather a run of commands and prohibitions that al-Mizan describes as several universal principles of the religion, following the earlier promise that this Quran guides to the way that is most upright. [1] They open by forbidding parents to kill their children out of fear of poverty, and answer that fear at once: God provides for parents and children alike, and such killing is a great iniquity. The passage then forbids even approaching fornication, calling it an indecency and an evil way, and forbids taking the life God has made inviolable except by right. Where a person is killed wrongfully, God grants the victim's heir an authority; Majma al-Bayan, citing Ibn Abbas, reads that authority as a choice between retaliation, blood-money, and pardon. [3]

From bloodshed the verses turn to trust and honesty: guard the orphan's property until he comes of age, keep every covenant, and give full measure with an even balance, for that is better and fairer in outcome. Then comes a command that reaches inward, not to pursue what one has no knowledge of, since hearing, sight, and the heart will each be questioned. The passage warns against walking the earth in arrogance: a person can neither split the earth apart nor rival the mountains in height, so pride is empty.

The evil of all this, the verses conclude, is detested by the Lord. al-Tibyan draws from this that God does not will acts of disobedience, against those who hold that He does. [7] These precepts are named wisdom that God revealed, sealed once more with the warning not to set up another god beside Him, on pain of being cast into Hell blamed and banished. The closing verse turns on the pagans of Mecca who assigned daughters to God while keeping sons for themselves, and calls their claim a monstrous word.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الحاج لا يملق أبدا … الإفلاس
narrations.chain: Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The pilgrim never becomes destitute. I asked, 'What is penury (imlaq)?' He said, 'Bankruptcy,' then he recited, 'Do not kill your children for the fear of penury.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: معصية ومقتاً فإن الله يمقته ويبغضه … وهو أشد النار عذاباً والزنا من أكبر الكبائر
narrations.chain: Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: It means disobedience and something loathed, for God loathes and hates it. As for 'an evil way,' it is the harshest of the Fire's punishment, and fornication is among the greatest of grave sins.

note.en: Majma al-Bayan, citing Ibn Abbas, reads the authority given to the victim's heir as a threefold choice: retaliation against the killer, blood-money, or pardon. [3]

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Kazim
narrations.arabic: نهى أن يقتل غير قاتله، أو يمثل بالقاتل … و أي نصرة أعظم من أن يدفع القاتل إلى أولياء المقتول فيقتله، و لا تبعة تلزمه من قتله في دين و لا دنيا
narrations.chain: Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan

text.en: He forbade killing anyone other than the murderer, or mutilating the murderer. And what greater help is there than that the murderer be handed over to the victim's heirs to be killed, with no liability upon them for it in religion or in this world?

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: هو الحسين بن علي (عليه السلام) قتل مظلوما و نحن أولياؤه، و القائم منا إذا قام طلب بثار الحسين … المقتول: الحسين (عليه السلام) و وليه: القائم
narrations.chain: Salam ibn al-Mustanir, from Abu Jafar

text.en: He is al-Husayn ibn Ali, killed wrongfully, and we are his heirs. The Qaim from among us, when he rises, will seek vengeance for al-Husayn. The one killed is al-Husayn, and his heir is the Qaim.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لا تفعل … أما سمعت الله عز و جل يقول: { إِنَّ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْبَصَرَ وَٱلْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُولـٰئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْؤُولاً }؟!
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Masada ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: A man said he sat long listening to his neighbours' singing-girls, protesting that it was only hearing with his ear. The Imam said, 'Do not do it,' then, 'Have you not heard God say, "Hearing, eyesight, and the heart, all of these are accountable"?'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يسأل السمع عما يسمع و البصر عما يطرف، و الفؤاد عما يعقد عليه
narrations.chain: al-Husayn ibn Harun, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The hearing is questioned about what it hears, the eyesight about what it looks upon, and the heart about what it resolves upon.

narrations.speaker: The Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: لا يزول قدم عبد يوم القيامة من بين يدي الله حتى يسأله عن أربع خصال عمرك فيما أفنيته وجسدك فيما أبليته ومالك من أين كسبته وأين وضعته وعن حبنا أهل البيت
narrations.chain: his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Jafar

text.en: No servant's foot will move on the Day of Resurrection, before God, until he is questioned about four things: his life, how he spent it; his body, how he wore it out; his wealth, whence he earned it and where he put it; and about love of us, the People of the House.

perspectives.en: On 'whoever is killed wrongfully,' the traditions diverge in application. Shia narrations in al-Burhan identify the one killed wrongfully as al-Husayn and his heir as the Qaim, who will rise to avenge him and will not be charged with excess. [19] Ibn Kathir instead reports Ibn Abbas reading the verse as foretelling Muawiya's rule: as the heir of the murdered Uthman, he was the assisted avenger who came to hold authority. [38] Both take the verse beyond a single homicide toward a claim about rightful vengeance, but they name opposite figures.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: عدة من كليات الدين يذكرها الله سبحانه وهي تتبع قوله قبل آيات { إن هذا القرآن يهدي للتي هي أقوم } الآية.

sources.gloss: Several universal principles of the religion that God mentions, following His earlier words, 'Indeed this Quran guides to that which is most upright.'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { فَقَدْ جَعَلْنَا لِوَلِيِّهِ سُلْطَاناً } أي قد أثبتنا لوليه سلطان القود على القاتل أو الدية أو العفو عن ابن عباس والضحاك

sources.gloss: 'We have given his heir an authority' means We have established for the heir authority of retaliation against the killer, or blood-money, or pardon; from Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفي ذلك دلالة على بطلان مذهب المجبرة من أنّ الله تعالى يريد المعاصي، لان هذه الآية صريحة بأن السيء من الافعال مكروه عند الله.

sources.gloss: In this is proof of the falsehood of the compulsionists' doctrine that God wills acts of disobedience, for this verse states plainly that the evil among deeds is detested by God.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: يقول معصية ومقتاً فإن الله يمقته ويبغضه … وهو أشد النار عذاباً والزنا من أكبر الكبائر.

sources.gloss: It means disobedience and something loathed, for God loathes and hates it; it is the harshest of the Fire's punishment, and fornication is among the greatest grave sins.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: لا يزول قدم عبد يوم القيامة من بين يدي الله حتى يسأله عن أربع خصال عمرك فيما أفنيته وجسدك فيما أبليته ومالك من أين كسبته وأين وضعته وعن حبنا أهل البيت

sources.gloss: No servant's foot will move on the Day of Resurrection until he is questioned about four things: his life and how he spent it, his body and how he wore it out, his wealth and where he earned and put it, and love of us, the People of the House.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: « الحاج لا يملق أبدا » ، قال: قلت: و ما الإملاق؟ قال: « الإفلاس »

sources.gloss: 'The pilgrim never becomes destitute.' I asked, 'What is penury (imlaq)?' He said, 'Bankruptcy.'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هو الحسين بن علي (عليه السلام) قتل مظلوما و نحن أولياؤه، و القائم منا إذا قام طلب بثار الحسين

sources.gloss: He is al-Husayn ibn Ali, killed wrongfully, and we are his heirs; the Qaim from among us, when he rises, will seek vengeance for al-Husayn.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يسأل السمع عما يسمع و البصر عما يطرف، و الفؤاد عما يعقد عليه

sources.gloss: The hearing is questioned about what it hears, the eyesight about what it looks upon, and the heart about what it resolves upon.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: وقد أخذ الإمام الحبر ابن عباس من عموم هذه الآية الكريمة ولاية معاوية السلطنة أنه سيملك لأنه كان ولي عثمان، وقد قتل مظلوماً

sources.gloss: Ibn Abbas derived from the generality of this verse Muawiya's authority to rule, since he was the heir of Uthman, who was killed wrongfully.

essay.en:
These verses press the surah's case for God's oneness against the Meccans who reject it. God has turned His proofs this way and that in the Quran so that people might take admonition, yet the same turning only drives the deniers further off. If it increases them only in aversion, why send it down? al-Tabrisi answers that its wisdom is to bind the proof and cut off every excuse, laying out the evidence that makes moral accountability sound [2].

Then comes a direct argument. Were there other gods besides Him, as the idolaters say, those gods would have encroached on the Lord of the Throne. al-Mizan reads this as their seeking a way to seize the sovereignty that none but He can hold, so the very supposition collapses; He is immaculate and greatly exalted above what they say [1]. The seven heavens, the earth, and every thing celebrate His praise, though people do not understand that glorification.

When the Prophet recites, God draws a hidden curtain, casts veils on their hearts, and a deafness into their ears. al-Tusi is careful here: this is a description and a rebuke of men who shut themselves against the truth, not God barring them from understanding, for that would be tasking them beyond their power, which He does not do [7]. God knows their real purpose in listening and their whispered slander that the Prophet is a bewitched man; by coining such epithets they only stray and cannot find a way [3].

The passage turns last to the resurrection they mock. Bones and dust brought back? Say: even stones or iron, or a creature more fantastic to your minds, the One who originated you the first time will remake you, for whoever can originate is the abler to restore [4]. They nod their heads and ask when. Say: maybe it is near, the day He calls and you respond, praising Him, thinking you lingered only a little.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: يعني و لقد ذكرنا عليا (عليه السلام) في القرآن و هو الذكر فما زادهم إلا نفورا
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Jafar

text.en: 'That they may take admonition' means: We mentioned Ali in the Quran, and he is the Reminder; yet it increased them only in aversion.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: تنقض الجدر تسبيحها
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Dawud al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Asked about 'there is not a thing but celebrates His praise, but you do not understand their glorification,' he said: 'The crumbling of the walls is their glorification.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: نعم، أما سمعت خشب البيت كيف ينقصف ، و ذلك تسبيحه، فسبحان الله على كل حال
narrations.chain: Masadah ibn Sadaqa, from Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father

text.en: A man asked: 'Does the dry tree glorify?' He said: 'Yes. Have you not heard the timber of the house cracking? That is its glorification. So glory to God in every state.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: الخلق الذي يكبر في صدوركم: الموت
narrations.chain: in the report of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: 'A creature more fantastic to your minds' - the creation that looms great in your breasts is death.

perspectives.en: Verse 46 ends with the deniers turning their backs 'when you mention your Lord alone.' Shia reports take this literally of reciting the Basmala aloud: the Prophet had the finest voice, and the Meccans fled when he reached 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim,' so this verse came down [20]. al-Tabari instead reads 'mention your Lord alone' as saying 'there is no god but God' during recitation, at which they withdrew in aversion; he notes a minority view that the ones who flee are the shaytans, but favors the deniers [31].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فقوله: { إذاً لابتغوا إلى ذي العرش سبيلاً } أي طلبوا سبيلاً إليه ليغلبوه على ما له من الملك

sources.gloss: His words 'they would surely have encroached on the Lord of the Throne' mean they sought a way to Him to overcome Him for the sovereignty He holds.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: الحكمة فيه إلزام الحجة وقطع المعذرة في إظهار الدلائل التي تحسن التكليف

sources.gloss: The wisdom in it is to bind the proof and cut off excuse by displaying the evidences that make moral responsibility sound.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { كيف ضربوا لك الأمثال } أي شبَّهوا لك الأشياء فقالوا مجنون وساحر وشاعر { فضلوا } بهذا القول عن الحق

sources.gloss: 'How they coin epithets for you' means they likened you to things, calling you mad, a sorcerer, a poet; by this speech they strayed from the truth.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قل يا محمد يحييكم من خلقكم أول مرة فإن من قدر على ابتداء الشيء كان على إعادته أقدر

sources.gloss: Say, Muhammad: the One who created you the first time revives you, for whoever has power to originate a thing is more able to bring it back.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وإِنما لم يجز المنع والحيلولة بينهم وبين ان يفقهوه، لأن ذلك تكليف ما لا يطاق، وذلك قبيح لا يجوز ان يفعله الله تعالى

sources.gloss: Barring them from understanding it is not permissible, for that would be tasking beyond capacity, an ugly thing that God does not do.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يعني و لقد ذكرنا عليا (عليه السلام) في القرآن و هو الذكر فما زادهم إلا نفورا

sources.gloss: It means We mentioned Ali in the Quran, and he is the Reminder; it increased them only in aversion.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قال: تنقض الجدر تسبيحها … نعم، أما سمعت خشب البيت كيف ينقصف ، و ذلك تسبيحه

sources.gloss: He said: the crumbling of the walls is their glorification … Yes, have you not heard the timber of the house cracking? That is its glorification.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: وهي الآية التي قال الله: { وَإِذَا ذَكَرْتَ رَبَّكَ فِي ٱلْقُرْءَانِ وَحْدَهُ } - بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم - { وَلَّوْاْ عَلَىٰ أَدْبَٰرِهِمْ نُفُوراً }

sources.gloss: This is the verse where God said 'when you mention your Lord alone' - that is, Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim - 'they turn their backs in aversion.'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و في رواية أبي الجارود، عن أبي جعفر (عليه السلام) قال: الخلق الذي يكبر في صدوركم: الموت

sources.gloss: In the report of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar: the creation that looms great in your breasts is death.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: { وَإذَا ذَكَرْتَ رَبَّكَ فـي القُرْآنِ وَحْدَهُ } يقول: وإذا قلت: لا إله إلا الله فـي القرآن وأنت تتلوه { وَلَّوْا علـى أدْبـارِهِمْ نُفُوراً }

sources.gloss: 'When you mention your Lord alone in the Quran' means: when you say 'there is no god but God' as you recite it, 'they turn their backs in aversion.'

title.en: The best word and false gods

essay.en:
These verses come in the middle of a Meccan sura addressed to a Prophet under attack, and they open with an order about speech: God tells him to have His servants 'speak in a manner which is the best.' Al-Mizan reads this best word as courteous speech, carrying fine manners and free of the harshness that lets Satan sow discord [1]. Majma al-Bayan records that the words came when the believers, worn down by their persecutors, asked leave to fight [3]. Judgment, the passage insists, belongs to God: He shows mercy or punishes as He wills, and the Prophet is 'not sent to watch over them' - al-Tusi explains that he was sent to call people to faith, not to force it [5]. God knows all in the heavens and the earth, has favoured some prophets over others, and gave David the Psalms, whose praise is itself the finest speech [1].

The argument then turns on the false gods. Invoke them, the verse says: they cannot remove distress or shift it. Al-Mizan notes that a true lord must be able to bring benefit and repel harm, which these cannot [2]. Those invoked - the angels, the Messiah, Uzayr [6] - are themselves servants seeking a means to their Lord, hoping for His mercy and fearing His punishment, so they are no gods at all. A warning follows: no town escapes destruction or severe punishment before the Resurrection, a decree inscribed in the Book, which al-Tusi identifies as the Preserved Tablet [7]. God withheld the signs Quraysh demanded, because earlier peoples denied such signs and were destroyed; Thamud's she-camel was a clear sign they wronged, and signs are sent only to warn. The passage closes with the vision God showed His Prophet and 'the tree cursed in the Quran,' set as a trial. Majma al-Bayan, with the narrations, names that tree the house of Umayya [4].

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi
narrations.arabic: إن الشيطان ينزغ بينهم … أي يدخل بينهم يحثهم على المعاصي

text.en: 'Satan incites ill feeling between them' means that he slips in among them and drives them on to acts of disobedience.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: سادة النّبييّن والمرسلين خمسة وهم أولو العزم من الرسل وعليهم دارت الرحى نوح وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى ومحمّد
narrations.chain: al-Kafi, from al-Sadiq

text.en: The masters of the prophets and messengers are five: they are the resolute messengers, on whom the mill turns - Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and Muhammad.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: كان يقول عند العلة … اللهم إنك عيرت أقواما فقلت … فيا من لا يملك كشف ضري و لا تحويله عني أحد غيره، صل على محمد و آل محمد، و اكشف ضري
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Ibn Faddal, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: At times of illness he would say: O Allah, You reproached certain peoples, saying this verse. So, O One besides whom no other can remove my harm or shift it from me, send blessings on Muhammad and his family, and lift my harm.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أنه سئل عن قوله تعالى … هو الفناء بالموت
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, in mursal form, from al-Sadiq

text.en: He was asked about this verse and said: it is annihilation by death.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إنما أمة محمد من الأمم، فمن مات فقد هلك
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: The community of Muhammad is one of the nations; whoever among them dies has perished.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: سأله قومه أن يأتيهم بآية، فنزل جبرئيل … و كنا إذا أرسلنا إلى قرية آية فلم يؤمنوا بها أهلكناهم، فلذلك أخرنا عن قومك الآيات
narrations.chain: in the report of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: His people asked Muhammad to bring them a sign, so Gabriel came down and said: when We used to send a town a sign and they did not believe in it, We destroyed them; so We have held the signs back from your people.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أصبح رسول الله … يوما حاسرا حزينا، فقيل له: مالك، يا رسول الله؟ فقال: إني رأيت الليلة صبيان بني أمية يرقون على منبري هذا، فقلت: يا رب معي؟ فقال: لا، و لكن بعدك
narrations.chain: from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: One morning the Messenger woke stricken and grieved. Asked what ailed him, he said: this night I saw the boys of Banu Umayya climbing this pulpit of mine. I said: My Lord, in my lifetime? He said: no, but after you.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: أخبرني عن قول الله … الأفجران من قريش، و من بني امية
narrations.chain: from Abu al-Tufayl

text.en: Ibn al-Kawwa asked him about God's words 'and the tree cursed in the Quran,' and he said: the two most iniquitous of Quraysh, and of Banu Umayya.

perspectives.en: On the closing verse the traditions divide. The Shia commentators, following the narrations, take the vision as the Prophet's dream of Banu Umayya climbing his pulpit and 'the tree cursed in the Quran' as that clan [4]. The Sunni reading is different: Ibn Kathir holds that the vision is the Night Journey to Jerusalem, which the deniers seized on, and that the cursed tree is the tree of Zaqqum; he mentions the Banu Umayya interpretation only to call it strange and weak [33].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: أي الكلمه التي هي أحسن، وهو اشتمالها على الأدب الجميل وتعريها عن الخشونة والشتم وسوء الأمر

sources.gloss: 'That which is best' means the word that is best: it carries fine manners and is free of harshness, abuse, and ill will.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: احتجاج من وجه آخر على التوحيد ونفي ربوبية الآلهة الذين يدعون من دون الله وأنهم لا يستطيعون كشف الضر ولا تحويله عن عبادهم

sources.gloss: A further argument for God's oneness, denying the lordship of the gods invoked besides Him: they cannot remove harm or shift it from their worshippers.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فيقولون يا رسول الله ائذن لنا في قتالهم

sources.gloss: They kept saying: Messenger of God, give us leave to fight them - the occasion Majma reports for this verse, from al-Kalbi.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقالوا على هذا التأويل إن الشجرة الملعونة في القرآن هي بنو أمية

sources.gloss: On this reading they said: the cursed tree in the Quran is Banu Umayya.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ما وكّلناك بمنعهم من الكفر بل أرسلناك داعياً لهم

sources.gloss: We did not entrust you with keeping them from disbelief; rather We sent you to call them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال ابن عباس والحسن { الذين من دونه } الملائكة والمسيح وعزير

sources.gloss: Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan said: 'those besides Him' are the angels, the Messiah, and Uzayr.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: مسطور في الكتاب يعني في اللوح المحفوظ

sources.gloss: It is inscribed in the Book, that is, in the Preserved Tablet.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: أي يدخل بينهم يحثهم على المعاصي

sources.gloss: That is, he slips in among them and incites them to acts of disobedience.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فيا من لا يملك كشف ضري و لا تحويله عني أحد غيره، صل على محمد و آل محمد، و اكشف ضري

sources.gloss: O One besides whom none can remove my harm or shift it from me, bless Muhammad and his family and lift my harm.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هو الفناء بالموت

sources.gloss: It is annihilation by death.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و كنا إذا أرسلنا إلى قرية آية فلم يؤمنوا بها أهلكناهم، فلذلك أخرنا عن قومك الآيات

sources.gloss: When We sent a town a sign and they did not believe in it, We destroyed them; so We held the signs back from your people.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إني رأيت الليلة صبيان بني أمية يرقون على منبري هذا

sources.gloss: This night I saw the boys of Banu Umayya climbing this pulpit of mine.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: سادة النّبييّن والمرسلين خمسة وهم أولو العزم من الرسل

sources.gloss: The masters of the prophets and messengers are five: they are the resolute messengers.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: وقيل المراد بالشجرة الملعونة بنو أمية، وهو غريب ضعيف

sources.gloss: It is said the cursed tree means Banu Umayya, but that is strange and weak.

title.en: Iblis and the Children of Adam

essay.en:
This passage, the seventh of the surah's twelve, returns to the story of Iblis. God told the angels to prostrate before Adam, and they all did but Iblis, who scorned bowing to one created from clay. Tusi notes that Iblis understood the command as marking Adam's rank above his own; had Adam been only a direction of prayer, the refusal would have made no sense [6]. Iblis then points to 'this one whom You have honoured above me' and vows, if he is respited until the Day of Resurrection, to lay his yoke on Adam's progeny except a few. Tabrisi glosses the verb as taking a thing entirely, the way locusts strip a field bare [3].

God answers: Begone; hell is the ample requital of all who follow him. The imperatives that come next - to incite with his voice, to rally cavalry and infantry, to share in wealth and children, and to make promises - Tusi reads not as permission granted but as a threat, in the manner of 'do what you will' [7]. And the verse itself adds that Satan promises them nothing but delusion. Over God's own servants, though, Iblis has no authority; the Lord suffices as trustee. Tabatabai takes 'My servants' to mean more than the sincere few, including all of Adam's descendants who are not led astray [1].

The surah then turns to its signs. Tabrisi notes that, after speaking of Satan and the idolaters, God argues against them through His works [4]: He drives the ships across the sea that people may seek His bounty; when distress strikes them there, everything they call upon vanishes except Him, yet once delivered to land they turn away, for man is ungrateful. A warning follows - that He could make the coastland swallow them, or loose a rain of stones, or return them to the sea and drown them, with no defender to be found.

The passage closes on honour. God has honoured the Children of Adam, carried them over land and sea, provided them good things, and preferred them above much of what He created. Tabatabai distinguishes the honouring, an intrinsic dignity given to humankind, from the preference, the added measure it enjoys over other creatures [2].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: ما كان من مال حرام فهو شرك الشيطان - قال - و يكون مع الرجل حتى يجامع، فيكون من نطفته و نطفة الرجل إذا كان حراما
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Whatever comes from unlawful wealth is Satan's share. And he is present with a man when he has intercourse, so the child is from his seed and the man's seed together, when it is unlawful.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أنه لما قال النبي (صلى الله عليه و آله) لعلي (عليه السلام) ما قال، و أقامه للناس، صرخ إبليس صرخة، فاجتمعت له العفاريت … فقال النبي (صلى الله عليه و آله): { بِسمِ ٱللهِ ٱلرَّحْمٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيـمِ... إِنَّ عِبَادِي لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطَانٌ }
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Jafar ibn Muhammad al-Khuzai, from his father, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When the Prophet said what he said about Ali and set him before the people, Iblis let out a cry and the demons gathered to him ... then the Prophet recited: 'As for My servants, you shall have no authority over them.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إن الله لا يكرم روح كافر، و لكن يكرم أرواح المؤمنين، و إنما كرامة النفس و الدم بالروح، و الرزق الطيب هو العلم
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Jafar ibn Ahmad, from Abd al-Karim ibn Abd al-Rahim, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Jafar

text.en: God does not honour the soul of a disbeliever, but He honours the souls of the believers. The dignity of the self and the blood is by the soul, and the good provision is knowledge.

perspectives.en: On 'preferred above much of what We created,' the traditions read the comparison differently. Ibn Kathir relates that this verse has been adduced as proof that the human species is superior to the angelic [37]. Tabrisi, by contrast, holds that it does not settle the matter: he does not deny that the prophets may surpass the angels, even if the angelic species as a whole is more excellent than the human species [5].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: المراد بعبادي أعم من المخلصين الذين استثناهم إبليس بقوله إلا قليلا بل غير الغاوين من أتباع أبليس

sources.gloss: By 'My servants' is meant more than the sincere whom Iblis excepted with 'except a few'; it includes those of Adam's descendants who are not led astray.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: المراد بالتكريم تخصيص الشيء بالعناية وتشريفه بما يختص به ولا يوجد في غيره وبذلك يفترق عن التفضيل فإن التكريم معنى نفسي

sources.gloss: The honouring means singling a thing out with special care and a dignity found in nothing else, and by this it differs from the preference, for the honouring is something intrinsic.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: الاحتناك الاقتطاع من الأصل يقال احتنك فلان ما عند فلان من مال أو علم إذا استقصاه فأخذه كله واحتنك الجراد الزرع إذا أكله كله

sources.gloss: Ihtinak means cutting off from the root: one says a man 'took entirely' another's wealth or knowledge when he took it all, and the locusts 'devoured' the crop when they ate it all.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: لمّا تقدَّم ذكر الشيطان وذكر المشركين وعبدة الأوثان احتجَّ عليهم سبحانه بدلائل التوحيد والإيمان

sources.gloss: Since the mention of Satan, the idolaters and the worshippers of idols had come before, God argued against them with the proofs of His oneness and of faith.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فغير منكر أن يكون الأنبياء أفضل من الملائكة وإن كان جنس الملائكة أفضل من جنس بني آدم

sources.gloss: It is not to be denied that the prophets may be more excellent than the angels, even if the angelic species as a whole is more excellent than the human species.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وذلك يدل على ان إِبليس فهم من ذلك الأمر تفضيله عليه، ولو كان بمنزلة القبلة لما كان لامتناعه عليه وجه

sources.gloss: This shows that Iblis understood from the command that Adam had been favoured over him; had Adam only been a direction of prayer, his refusal would have had no ground.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: صورته صورة الأمر والمراد به التهديد، وجرى مجرى قوله اعملوا ما شئتم

sources.gloss: Its form is that of a command, but a threat is intended, along the lines of His words 'do what you will.'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ما كان من مال حرام فهو شرك الشيطان - قال - و يكون مع الرجل حتى يجامع، فيكون من نطفته و نطفة الرجل إذا كان حراما

sources.gloss: Whatever comes from unlawful wealth is Satan's share; and he is present with a man when he has intercourse, so the child comes from his seed and the man's when it is unlawful.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فقال النبي (صلى الله عليه و آله): { بِسمِ ٱللهِ ٱلرَّحْمٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيـمِ... إِنَّ عِبَادِي لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطَانٌ }

sources.gloss: Then the Prophet recited: 'In the name of God... As for My servants, you shall have no authority over them.'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن الله لا يكرم روح كافر، و لكن يكرم أرواح المؤمنين، و إنما كرامة النفس و الدم بالروح، و الرزق الطيب هو العلم

sources.gloss: God does not honour the soul of a disbeliever but honours the souls of the believers; the dignity of the self and the blood is by the soul, and the good provision is knowledge.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: وقد استدل بهذه الآية الكريمة على أفضلية جنس البشر على جنس الملائكة

sources.gloss: This noble verse has been adduced as evidence for the superiority of the human species over the angelic species.

title.en: The imam and the Prophet's steadfastness

essay.en:
The passage sets the Day of Resurrection before us: God will summon every group of people along with their imam [1]. Tabatabai reads this imam as the leader a people followed, whether one of guidance or one of misguidance, so that each follower is brought forward together with the one he took as his guide [1]. Those handed their record in the right hand read it and are not wronged in the least; Tabrisi notes that receiving the record in the right hand is the mark of acceptance and deliverance [3]. Verse 72 states the reverse: whoever was blind to the truth in this world - blind in insight, not in sight [1] - is blinder still, and further astray, in the Hereafter.

The passage then turns to the Prophet. The idolaters nearly lured him away from what was revealed, hoping he would attribute to God something other than it [2]. Tabatabai explains that the fortifying named next is divine protection, and the wording shows he neither inclined toward them nor came near it [2]; Tabrisi likewise reads it as the steadying of his heart upon the truth through prophethood and the miracles [4]. Had he leaned even a little, a doubled punishment in this life and the next would have followed [2]. Finally the idolaters nearly drove him from Mecca; had they done so, they themselves would not have remained long after him - the abiding way God has followed with the messengers before him [2].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: يجيء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله في فرقة وعلى في فرقة والحسن في فرقة والحسين في فرقة وكل من مات بين ظهراني قوم جاؤوا معه
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i ibn Abdillah, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: The Messenger of God will come amid a group, Ali amid a group, al-Hasan amid a group, al-Husayn amid a group; and everyone who died among a people comes together with him.

narrations.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: يدعى كل قوم بإمام زمانهم، و كتاب ربهم، و سنة نبيهم
narrations.chain: al-Rida, from his fathers, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, from the Messenger of God

text.en: Each people will be summoned by the imam of their age, the book of their Lord, and the sunna of their prophet.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يا فضيل، اعرف إمامك، فإنك إذا عرفت إمامك لم يضرك تقدم هذا الأمر أو تأخر، و من عرف إمامه ثم مات قبل أن يقوم صاحب هذا الأمر، كان بمنزلة من كان قاعدا في عسكره
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: O Fudayl, know your imam. If you know your imam, it will not harm you whether this affair comes sooner or later. Whoever knows his imam, then dies before the one who rises appears, is like one seated in his army camp.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ذلك الذي يسوف نفسه الحج- يعني حجة الإسلام- حتى يأتيه الموت
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir

text.en: That is the one who keeps putting off his hajj - meaning the obligatory hajj - until death comes to him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: من لم يدله خلق السماوات و الأرض، و اختلاف الليل و النهار، و دوران الفلك … على أن وراء ذلك أمرا أعظم منه
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: Whoever is not led by the creation of the heavens and earth, the alternation of night and day, and the turning of the heavens to the fact that beyond them lies something greater - he is blind in the Hereafter and further astray.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: تفسيرها في علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام: ولقد أرادوا أن يردوك عن الذي أوحينا إليك في علي، ان الله أوحى إليه أن أمرهم بولاية علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام
narrations.chain: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Fazari, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: Its interpretation concerns Ali ibn Abi Talib: they wanted to turn you back from what We revealed to you regarding Ali, for God had revealed to him to command them with the wilaya of Ali ibn Abi Talib.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: هذا مما نزل بإياك أعني و اسمعي يا جارة خاطب الله عز و جل بذلك نبيه (صلى الله عليه و آله) و أراد به أمته
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Tamim ibn Abdillah al-Qurashi, from his father, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Jahm, from al-Rida

text.en: This was revealed in the manner of 'I mean you, but hear it, O neighbour': God addressed His Prophet by it but intended the community - as with 'If you associate, your work will fail,' and 'Had We not fortified you, you might have inclined toward them a little.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: هي سنة محمد (صلى الله عليه و آله) و من كان قبله من الرسل، و هو الإسلام
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: It is the sunna of Muhammad and of the messengers before him, and it is Islam.

perspectives.en: On verse 71 the traditions read 'imam' differently. Tabatabai holds it means the leader a people followed, whether of guidance or misguidance [1], and the Shia narrations identify that leader as the Imam of each age, the Prophet and the Imams of his household [14]. Sunni readings vary: Tabari judges best the imam whom people followed in this world [22], while Ibn Kathir holds the strongest sense to be the record of deeds, since God calls the register a clear imam [29]. All agree that whom one follows here decides one's standing then.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فالظاهر أن المراد بإمام كل أُناس في الآية من ائتموا به سواء كان إمام حق أو إمام باطل

sources.gloss: So what is apparently meant by the imam of each people in the verse is the one they followed, whether an imam of truth or an imam of falsehood.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: التثبيت - كما يفيده السياق - هو العصمة الإلهية … دليل على أنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لم يركن ولم يكد

sources.gloss: The fortifying, as the context indicates, is divine protection - a proof that he neither inclined toward them nor came near it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: جعل الله إعطاء الكتاب باليمين علامة الرضا والخلاص

sources.gloss: God made the giving of the record in the right hand a sign of acceptance and deliverance.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ولولا أن ثبتناك أي ثبتنا قلبك على الحق والرشد بالنبوة والعصمة والمعجزات

sources.gloss: 'Had We not fortified you' means: had We not steadied your heart upon truth and right guidance through prophethood, protection, and the miracles.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: يجيء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله في فرقة وعلى في فرقة والحسن في فرقة والحسين في فرقة وكل من مات بين ظهراني قوم جاؤوا معه

sources.gloss: The Messenger of God comes amid a group, Ali amid a group, al-Hasan amid a group, al-Husayn amid a group; and everyone who died among a people comes with him.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يدعى كل قوم بإمام زمانهم، و كتاب ربهم، و سنة نبيهم

sources.gloss: Each people is summoned by the imam of their age, the book of their Lord, and the sunna of their prophet.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ذلك الذي يسوف نفسه الحج- يعني حجة الإسلام- حتى يأتيه الموت

sources.gloss: That is the one who keeps putting off his hajj - meaning the obligatory hajj - until death comes to him.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هذا مما نزل بإياك أعني و اسمعي يا جارة خاطب الله عز و جل بذلك نبيه (صلى الله عليه و آله) و أراد به أمته

sources.gloss: This was revealed in the manner of 'I mean you but let the neighbour hear': God addressed His Prophet by it but intended the community.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هي سنة محمد (صلى الله عليه و آله) و من كان قبله من الرسل، و هو الإسلام

sources.gloss: It is the sunna of Muhammad and of the messengers before him, and it is Islam.

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: تفسيرها في علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام: ولقد أرادوا أن يردوك عن الذي أوحينا إليك في علي

sources.gloss: Its interpretation concerns Ali ibn Abi Talib: they wanted to turn you back from what We revealed to you concerning Ali.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: وأولـى هذه الأقوال عندنا بـالصواب، قول من قال: معنى ذلك: يوم ندعو كلّ أناس بإمامهم الذي كانوا يقتدون به، ويأتـمُّون به فـي الدنـيا

sources.gloss: The best of these views to us is that it means: the Day We summon every people by the imam whom they followed and took as their leader in this world.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: ولكن المراد ههنا بالإمام هو كتاب الأعمال

sources.gloss: But what is meant here by the imam is the record of deeds.

title.en: Prayer, the Quran, and human nature

essay.en: The passage opens by commanding the Prophet to establish the prayer from the sun's decline until the darkness of night, and to keep the dawn recital, which is attended by angels. Reading the sun's decline as its passing the meridian and the darkness of night as midnight, the Shia commentators take the verse to gather the times of four daily prayers, while the dawn recital names the fifth [3]. Next comes the night vigil, a devotion laid upon the Prophet alone, tied to the promise that his Lord will raise him to a praiseworthy station, which the reports read as the great intercession on the Day of Resurrection [1]. The Prophet is then taught to ask for a worthy entrance and a worthy departure and a helping authority, and to proclaim that the truth has come and falsehood has vanished. The passage turns to the Quran itself, sent down as a cure and a mercy for the faithful while it only increases the wrongdoers in loss; al-Mizan explains that it heals the diseases of the heart as medicine heals the body [2]. It closes with the human pattern of turning aside when blessed and despairing when harmed, which al-Mizan reads as the state of a man absorbed in secondary causes [2], and with the reminder that everyone acts according to his own character, while God knows best who is better guided.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: خمس صلوات في الليل و النهار … و دلوكها: زوالها، ففيما بين دلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل أربع صلوات، سماهن الله و بينهن و وقتهن، و غسق الليل هو انتصافه
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Five prayers in the night and day. The sun's decline is its passing the meridian; between the sun's decline and the darkness of night are four prayers, which God named, set out, and timed; and the darkness of night is its midpoint.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن ملائكة الليل تصعد و ملائكة النهار تنزل عند طلوع الفجر، فأنا أحب أن تشهد ملائكة الليل و ملائكة النهار صلاتي
narrations.chain: al-Tusi in his Majalis, by his chain from Ruzayq, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The angels of the night ascend and the angels of the day descend at the break of dawn, so I love that the angels of the night and the angels of the day witness my prayer.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: لو قد قمت المقام المحمود لشفعت في أبي وأمي وعمي وأخ كان لي في الجاهلية
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya and Hisham, from Abu Abdillah, from the Messenger of Allah

text.en: Once I stand at the praiseworthy station, I will intercede for my father, my mother, my uncle, and a brother of mine from the age of ignorance.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: يا علي، إن ربي عز و جل ملكني الشفاعة في أهل التوحيد من امتي، و حظر ذلك على من ناصبك أو ناصب ولدك من بعدك
narrations.chain: al-Tusi in his Amali, by his chain from Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah

text.en: O Ali, my Lord has granted me intercession for the people of monotheism among my community, and has withheld it from whoever bore enmity toward you or toward your children after you.

note.en: Al-Qummi reports this prayer came down at the conquest of Mecca, as the Prophet was about to enter it [10]; al-Mizan instead reads it broadly, as the plea of the truthful in every entrance and exit [1].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إذا قام القائم أذهب دولة الباطل
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Jafar

text.en: When the Qaim rises, he will do away with the reign of falsehood.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إنما الشفاء في علم القرآن، لقوله: { مَا هُوَ شِفَآءٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ } لأهله، لا شك فيه و لا مرية، فأهله أئمة الهدى
narrations.chain: from Masada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The healing lies only in the knowledge of the Quran, by His words 'that which is a cure and mercy' for its people, without doubt or dispute; and its people are the Imams of guidance.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: نزل جبرئيل على محمد صلى الله عليه و آله بهذه الآية { وَلاَ يَزِيدُ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ } آل محمد حقهم { إِلاَّ خَسَاراً }
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, raising it to Abu Jafar

text.en: Gabriel brought down this verse to Muhammad: 'and it increases the wrongdoers' - those who deny the family of Muhammad their right - 'only in loss.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: النية أفضل من العمل، ألا و إن النية هي العمل، ثم قرأ قوله عز و جل { قُلْ كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ عَلَىٰ شَاكِلَتِهِ } يعني على نيته
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Minqari, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Intention is better than the deed; indeed, intention is the deed. Then he recited 'Everyone acts according to his character' - meaning according to his intention.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: صَلِّ فِيهَا قَدْ رَأَيْتُهَا مَا أَنْظَفَهَا … أَ مَا تَقْرَأُ اَلْقُرْآنَ قُلْ كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ عَلىٰ شٰاكِلَتِهِ فَرَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ هُوَ أَهْدىٰ سَبِيلاً صَلِّ عَلَى اَلْقِبْلَةِ وَ غَرِّبْهُمْ
narrations.chain: from Fadala, from Hammad al-Nab, from al-Hakam ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Pray in them - I have seen them, how clean they are. Do you not read the Quran, 'Everyone acts according to his character; your Lord knows best who is better guided'? Pray toward the qibla and leave them be.

perspectives.en: On verse 78 the traditions read the times differently. Following the Imams, the Shia commentators take the sun's decline as its noon passing and the darkness of night as midnight, so the verse fixes all five daily prayers and gives Zuhr and Asr, then Maghrib and Isha, shared time windows [3]. Al-Tabari records that the early authorities disagreed even over the sun's decline: some, like Ibn Masud, read it as sunset, making the verse begin with Maghrib, while others read it as the noon passing, which al-Tabari himself preferred [22]. Both traditions agree the dawn recital is the Fajr prayer, witnessed by the angels of night and day.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: ولذا فسروا المقام المحمود بأنه المقام الذي يحمده عليه جميع الخلائق وهو مقام الشفاعة الكبرى له صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يوم القيامة

sources.gloss: This is why they explained the praiseworthy station as the station all creatures praise: the great intercession granted to the Prophet on the Day of Resurrection.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وعد القرآن شفاء والشفاء إنما يكون عن مرض دليل على أن للقلوب أحوالاً نسبة القرآن إليها نسبة الدواء الشافي إلى المرض

sources.gloss: Calling the Quran a cure, and a cure is only for a disease, shows that hearts have states to which the Quran stands as healing medicine stands to illness.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فصلاتا دلوك الشمس الظهر والعصر وصلاتا غسق الليل هما المغرب والعشاء الآخر والمراد بقرآن الفجر صلاة الفجر فهذه خمس صلوات

sources.gloss: The two prayers of the sun's decline are Zuhr and Asr, the two of the night's darkness are Maghrib and Isha, and the dawn recital is the Fajr prayer - so these are five prayers.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: لو قد قمت المقام المحمود لشفعت في أبي وأمي وعمي وأخ كان لي في الجاهلية

sources.gloss: Once I stand at the praiseworthy station, I will intercede for my father, my mother, my uncle, and a brother of mine from the age of ignorance.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: نزلت يوم فتح مكة لما أراد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله دخولها

sources.gloss: It was revealed on the day of the conquest of Mecca, when the Messenger of Allah intended to enter it.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و دلوكها: زوالها، ففيما بين دلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل أربع صلوات، سماهن الله و بينهن و وقتهن، و غسق الليل هو انتصافه

sources.gloss: Its decline is its passing the meridian; between the sun's decline and the darkness of night are four prayers, which God named, set out, and timed; and the darkness of night is its midpoint.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن ربي عز و جل ملكني الشفاعة في أهل التوحيد من امتي، و حظر ذلك على من ناصبك أو ناصب ولدك من بعدك

sources.gloss: My Lord has granted me intercession for the people of monotheism among my community, and has withheld it from whoever bore enmity toward you or your children after you.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إذا قام القائم أذهب دولة الباطل

sources.gloss: When the Qaim rises, he will do away with the reign of falsehood.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إنما الشفاء في علم القرآن

sources.gloss: The healing lies only in the knowledge of the Quran.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: النية أفضل من العمل، ألا و إن النية هي العمل

sources.gloss: Intention is better than the deed; indeed, intention is the deed.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: واختلف أهل التأويـل فـي الوقت الذي عناه الله بدلوك الشمس، فقال بعضهم: هو وقت غروبها

sources.gloss: The exegetes differed over the time meant by the sun's decline; some of them said it is the time of its setting.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. al-hasan al-tusi

excerpt.text: صَلِّ فِيهَا قَدْ رَأَيْتُهَا مَا أَنْظَفَهَا

sources.gloss: Pray in them - I have seen them, how clean they are!

essay.en:
The passage opens with a question put to the Prophet about the Spirit, and the answer that the Spirit belongs to the command of his Lord, and that people have been given only a little knowledge [2]. Commentators read the Spirit in more than one way: the soul that gives the body life, which the questioners were left without an answer about as a test; the Quran itself; or a mighty creation [2][4]. Tabatabai reads it as belonging to God's command, the word 'Be' by which a thing comes to exist without intermediate causes, so the Spirit is of the realm of the command rather than of gradual making [1].

The next verses turn to the Prophet himself. God could take away what He has revealed, and no one could recover it for him against God, were it not for a mercy from his Lord, whose grace to him has been great [2]. Then comes the challenge: were all humans and jinn to combine, they could not bring the like of this Quran, even helping one another [2]. And though God has set out every kind of parable in it, most people answer only with ingratitude.

The passage closes with the demands of the Meccan chiefs [3]: make a spring gush from the ground, own a garden with rivers running through it, drop the sky in fragments, bring God and the angels into view, hold a house of gold, or climb into the sky and bring down a book they can read. Tabatabai notes that some demands lie beyond any created power and some are impossible in themselves, such as bringing God and the angels, and that they addressed them to the Prophet as though the unseen power were his own [1]. The reply sets this straight: Immaculate is my Lord; am I anything but a human apostle? As a man he holds none of this power, and as an apostle his task is only to deliver [1].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: خلق أعظم من جبرئيل (عليه السلام) و ميكائيل، كان مع رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله)، و هو مع الأئمة، و هو من الملكوت
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abi Basir

text.en: A creation greater than Jibril and Mikail. It was with the Messenger of God, and it is with the Imams, and it is of the malakut.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: جبرئيل (عليه السلام) من الملائكة، و الروح غير جبرئيل … و الروح غير الملائكة
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Ala, from Sad al-Iskaf

text.en: Jibril is one of the angels, and the Spirit is other than Jibril. The Spirit is other than the angels.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الله تبارك و تعالى أحد صمد، و الصمد: الشيء الذي ليس له جوف، فإنما الروح خلق من خلقه، له بصر و قوة و تأييد، يجعله في قلوب الرسل و المؤمنين
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Zurara and Humran, from Abi Jafar and Abi Abdillah

text.en: God is One, Eternal; the Eternal is that which has no cavity. The Spirit is a creation of His creation; it has sight, power and support. He places it in the hearts of the messengers and the believers.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
