narrations.arabic: و قد يعلم ما لا يريده أبدا، و ذلك قوله عز و جل: { وَلَئِن شِئْنَا لَنَذْهَبَنَّ بِٱلَّذِي أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ } فهو يعلم كيف يذهب به و هو لا يذهب به أبدا
narrations.chain: from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Nawfali, on the debate of Sulayman al-Marwazi with al-Rida

text.en: He may know what He never wills. That is His saying, 'If We wish, We would take away what We have revealed to you.' He knows how He would take it away, yet He will never take it away.

narrations.speaker: Ibn Abbas
narrations.arabic: يريد حيث جعلك سيد ولد آدم و ختم بك النبيين و أعطاك المقام المحمود
narrations.chain: al-Tabrisi in Majma al-Bayan, from Ibn Abbas

text.en: He means: since He made you the master of the children of Adam, sealed the prophets with you, and gave you the Praised Station.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى أَنْزَلَ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ بِهَذِهِ الْحُرُوفِ الَّتِي يَتَدَاوَلُهَا جَمِيعُ الْعَرَبِ ثُمَّ قَالَ: «قُلْ لَئِنِ اجْتَمَعَتِ الإِنْسُ وَالْجِنُّ عَلى أَنْ يَأْتُوا بِمِثْلِ هذَا الْقُرْآنِ لا يَأْتُونَ بِمِثْلِهِ وَلَوْ كانَ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ ظَهِيراً»
narrations.chain: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhdhal, from his father, from Abi al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida

text.en: God revealed this Quran with these very letters that all the Arabs use among themselves. Then He said: 'Say, should all humans and jinn rally to bring the like of this Quran, they will not bring its like, even if they assisted one another.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: نزل جبرئيل بهذه الآية هكذا: { فَأَبَىٰ أَكْثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ } بولاية علي { إِلاَّ كُفُوراً }
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abi Hamza, from Abi Jafar

text.en: Jibril brought this verse down thus: 'but most people, concerning the guardianship of Ali, refused all but ingratitude.'

note.en: These demands were made in Mecca before the migration by Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya, the brother of Umm Salama [9].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعاً يعني عيناً أو تكون لك جنة يعني بستاناً من نخيل وعنب … يقول من الله إلى عبد الله بن أبي أمية أن محمداً صادق وإني أنا بعثته ويجيء معه أربعة من الملائكة يشهدون أن الله هو كتبه
narrations.chain: in the report of Abu al-Jarud, from Abi Jafar

text.en: 'A spring' means a flowing spring, and 'a garden' means an orchard of date palms and vines. The book they demand would be a message from God to Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya that Muhammad is truthful and that He sent him, brought by four angels who witness that God wrote it.

perspectives.en: Sunni and Shia commentators agree that the question about the Spirit reached the Prophet through the Jews and that its inner reality was left with God. They differ on what it is. al-Tabari records that the questioners were a group of Jews, and al-Qurtubi judges that leaving the Spirit undefined is the sound view, since God calls it a matter of His command [18][30]. The Shia narrations are more specific: reporting from the Imams, they call the Spirit a creation greater than Jibril and Mikail, distinct from the angels, which accompanied the Prophet and remains with the Imams [10].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: أما قوله: { بشراً } فليرد به اقتراحهم عليه أن يأتي بهذه الآيات عن قدرته في نفسه، وأما قوله: { رسولاً } فليرد به اقتراح ايتائها عن قدرة مكتسبة من ربه

sources.gloss: The word 'human' answers their demand that he bring these signs by his own power, and the word 'apostle' answers the demand that he bring them by a power gained from his Lord.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: اختلف في الروح المسؤول عنه على أقوال أحدها: أنهم سألوه عن الروح الذي هو في بدن الإنسان ما هو ولم يجبهم

sources.gloss: They differed about the Spirit asked about, into several views; one is that they asked about the spirit in the human body, and he did not answer them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: اجتمعوا عند الكعبة وقال بعضهم ابعثوا إلى محمد فكلِّموه وخاصموه

sources.gloss: They gathered at the Kaba, and some of them said: send for Muhammad, speak with him and dispute with him.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: واختلفوا في الروح الذي سألوا عنه. فقال ابن عباس: هو جبرائيل … وقيل: هو روح الحيوان، وهو الاظهر في الكلام

sources.gloss: They differed about the Spirit they asked about: Ibn Abbas said it is Jibril; and it was said it is the animal spirit, which is the more apparent meaning.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: نزلت في عبد الله بن أبي أمية أخي أم سلمة رحمة الله عليها وذلك أنه قال هذا لرسول الله بمكة قبل الهجرة

sources.gloss: It was revealed about Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya, brother of Umm Salama, and that is because he said this to the Messenger in Mecca before the migration.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: خلق أعظم من جبرئيل (عليه السلام) و ميكائيل، كان مع رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله)، و هو مع الأئمة، و هو من الملكوت

sources.gloss: A creation greater than Jibril and Mikail; it was with the Messenger of God, and it is with the Imams, and it is of the malakut.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و قد يعلم ما لا يريده أبدا … فهو يعلم كيف يذهب به و هو لا يذهب به أبدا

sources.gloss: He may know what He never wills; He knows how He would take it away, yet He will never take it away.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يريد حيث جعلك سيد ولد آدم و ختم بك النبيين و أعطاك المقام المحمود

sources.gloss: He means: since He made you the master of the children of Adam, sealed the prophets with you, and gave you the Praised Station.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: نزل جبرئيل بهذه الآية هكذا: { فَأَبَىٰ أَكْثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ } بولاية علي { إِلاَّ كُفُوراً }

sources.gloss: Jibril brought this verse down thus: 'but most people, concerning the guardianship of Ali, refused all but ingratitude.'

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: وذُكِر أن الذين سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الروح، فنزلت هذه الآية بـمسألتهم إياه عنها، كانوا قوماً من الـيهود

sources.gloss: It is mentioned that those who asked the Messenger about the Spirit, at whose asking this verse was revealed, were a group of Jews.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: والصحيح الإبهام لقوله: «قل الروح من أمر ربي»

sources.gloss: The sound view is to leave it undefined, because of His saying, 'the Spirit is of my Lord's command.'

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى أَنْزَلَ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ بِهَذِهِ الْحُرُوفِ الَّتِي يَتَدَاوَلُهَا جَمِيعُ الْعَرَبِ

sources.gloss: God revealed this Quran with these very letters that all the Arabs use among themselves.

title.en: A human messenger, not an angel

essay.en: The passage opens by naming the one thing that held people back from faith when guidance reached them: their objection that God would not send a human being as His apostle. The reply comes in a run of three verses that each close on the word 'apostle.' Tabatabai reads the second verse as an argument from the nature of earthly life: because human life is bound to the earth, its guidance can descend only through revelation from heaven, and had angels themselves dwelt on earth and lived there, God would have sent down to them an angel as apostle [1]. The next verse answers Quraysh over who could vouch for his mission; Tusi notes it answers their demand to know who would witness that he is God's messenger, and the reply is that God suffices, for He knows His servants inwardly and outwardly [4]. The tone then hardens. Whoever God guides is guided, and those He leaves astray have no guardian besides Him; Tabrisi explains that they are dragged on their faces to the Fire as a person is dragged in this world when he is utterly humiliated [3]. Their punishment is the requital for denying that bones and dust could be raised anew, though the One who created the heavens and the earth can create their like. The passage closes by exposing the greed behind their demands: even if they held the treasuries of their Lord's mercy they would hoard them for fear of spending, for man is very niggardly [6].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قالوا: إن الجن كانوا في الأرض قبلنا فبعث الله إليهم ملكا، فلو أراد الله أن يبعث إلينا لبعث ملكا من الملائكة
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abi al-Daylam, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: They said: the jinn were on the earth before us, and God sent them an angel; so had God wished to send to us, He would have sent an angel from among the angels.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: يا محمد إني رسول الله إليك أخبرك أن تكون ملكاً رسولاً أحب إليك أو تكون عبداً رسولاً … فقال جبرائيل: بل كن عبداً رسولاً، فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله: بل أكون عبداً رسولاً
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: An angel came to the Prophet and said: I am God's messenger to you; do you prefer to be a king and messenger, or a servant and messenger? Gabriel said: Rather be a servant and messenger. So the Messenger of God said: Rather I will be a servant and messenger.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn
narrations.arabic: إن في جهنم وادياً يقال له سعير إذا خبت جهنم فتح سعيرها وهو قوله: كلما خبت زدناهم سعيراً أي كلما انطفت
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sayf ibn Umayra, raising it to Ali ibn al-Husayn

text.en: In Hell there is a valley called Sa'ir; whenever Hell subsides, its Sa'ir is opened. That is His words, 'Whenever it subsides, We shall intensify the blaze for them,' meaning whenever it dies down.

perspectives.en: On verse 97 the traditions read the guidance and misguidance differently. Tusi holds that God's leading a person astray means He names him astray and withholds help because of the man's own bad choice, so no ally he takes can lift that name from him [5]. Razi records that his own companions cited this verse for their doctrine that God decrees guidance and misguidance outright, while the Mu'tazila read the leading-astray as withholding grace or barring the path to Paradise [33]. The Shia reading keeps the person's free choice as the ground of his ruin.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فالبشر القاطنون في الأرض لا غنى لهم عن وحي سماوي بنزول ملك رسول إليهم ويختص بذلك نبيهم

sources.gloss: The human beings who dwell on the earth cannot do without a heavenly revelation by the descent of an angel-messenger to them, and it is their prophet who is singled out for that.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي يسحبون على وجوههم إلى النار كما يفعل في الدنيا بمن يبالغ في إهانته وتعذيبه

sources.gloss: That is, they are dragged on their faces to the Fire, as is done in this world to one whom people go to great lengths to humiliate and torment.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وإِنما قال هذا جوابا لهم حين قالوا: من يشهد لك بأنك رسول الله؟ فقال الله له { قل كفى بالله شهيداً }

sources.gloss: He said this only in answer to them when they asked: who witnesses for you that you are God's messenger? So God told him: Say, God suffices as witness.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: من يحكم الله بضلاله وتسميته ضالاً بسوء اختياره للضلالة فإِنه لا ينفعه ولاية وليّ له

sources.gloss: Whom God rules to be astray and names astray because of his own bad choice of misguidance; no guardianship of any ally benefits him.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فاعلمهم الله أَنهم لو ملكوا خزائن الله، لأمسكوا بخلا بها وشحّاً خشية نفادها

sources.gloss: God informed them that had they possessed God's treasuries, they would have withheld them out of miserliness and greed, fearing they would run out.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: أخبرك أن تكون ملكاً رسولاً أحب إليك أو تكون عبداً رسولاً

sources.gloss: I tell you: do you prefer to be a king and messenger, or to be a servant and messenger?

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن الجن كانوا في الأرض قبلنا فبعث الله إليهم ملكا، فلو أراد الله أن يبعث إلينا لبعث ملكا من الملائكة

sources.gloss: The jinn were on the earth before us, and God sent them an angel; so had God wished to send to us, He would have sent an angel from among the angels.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: واحتج أصحابنا بهذه الآية على صحة مذهبهم في الهدى والضلال والمعتزلة حملوا هذا الإضلال تارة على الإضلال عن طريق الجنة وتارة على منع الألطاف

sources.gloss: Our companions used this verse as proof for their doctrine on guidance and misguidance; the Mu'tazila interpreted this leading-astray sometimes as misguidance from the path of Paradise, and sometimes as the withholding of graces.

essay.en:
These verses close Surah al-Israa by turning from the Prophet's opponents to a mirror of them in the past. Certainly We gave Moses nine manifest signs, yet Pharaoh dismissed him as bewitched, much as the Meccans turn from the Quran and demand other signs. Commentators differ over which nine are meant; among the lists reported are the hand, the staff, the tongue, the sea, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood [2]. Moses answers that Pharaoh already knows these came only from the Lord of the heavens and the earth; a reading traced to Ali gives the verb as 'I certainly know' rather than 'you know', so that it is Moses who affirms his own knowledge [4].

Pharaoh wanted to drive them from the land, so God drowned him and all who were with him and settled the Children of Israel in his place. When the occasion of the other promise comes, God will gather them in mixed company.

The passage then returns to the Quran itself. With the truth it was sent down, and the Prophet is only a bearer of good news and a warner. It was sent in separate parts, not all at once, across some twenty years, so people could receive it gradually [3]. Those given knowledge before it fall on their faces in prostration when it is recited, weeping, and it increases them in humility.

Say: invoke 'Allah' or invoke 'the All-beneficent'; whichever Name is used, all the Best Names are His. Tabatabai calls this among the Quran's most radiant verses: a name is only a path to the One named, so calling by many names remains the worship of one God, against the idolaters who scatter worship among names [1]. The occasion, Tusi records, was that the polytheists heard the Prophet name God as both Allah and al-Rahman and supposed he called on two gods [8]. The surah ends as it began, in glorification: praise Allah who has taken no son and has no partner, and magnify Him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Kazim
narrations.arabic: قالوا: أخبرنا عن الآيات التسع التي أوتيها موسى بن عمران. قلت: العصا، و إخراجه يده من جيبه بيضاء، و الجراد، و القمل، و الضفادع، و الدم، و رفع الطور، و المن و السلوى آية واحدة، و فلق البحر. قالوا: صدقت
narrations.chain: Abdullah ibn Jafar al-Himyari, from al-Hasan ibn Zarif, from Mamar, from al-Rida, from his father Musa ibn Jafar

text.en: They said: tell us about the nine signs given to Moses son of Imran. I said: the staff, his bringing his hand white from his bosom, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the raising of the Mount, manna and quails as one sign, and the splitting of the sea. They said: you have spoken truly.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: سئل أبو عبد الله (عليه السلام) عمن بجبهته علة لا يقدر على السجود عليها. قال: يضع ذقنه على الأرض، إن الله عز و جل يقول: { يَخِرُّونَ لِلأَذْقَانِ سُجَّداً }
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, by his chain

text.en: He was asked about someone with an ailment on his forehead who cannot prostrate on it. He said: he places his chin on the ground, for God, Mighty and Majestic, says, 'they fall down on their faces in prostration.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قلت لأبي عبد الله (عليه السلام): على الإمام أن يسمع من خلفه و إن كثروا؟ فقال: ليقرأ قراءة وسطا، يقول الله تبارك و تعالى: { وَلاَ تَجْهَرْ بِصَلاَتِكَ وَلاَ تُخَافِتْ بِهَا }
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan

text.en: I asked him: must the prayer-leader make those behind him hear, even if they are many? He said: let him recite in a middle voice; God, blessed and exalted, says, 'Be neither loud in your prayer, nor murmur it.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: تفسيرها: و لا تجهر بولاية علي (عليه السلام) و لا بما أكرمته به حتى آمرك بذلك { وَلاَ تُخَافِتْ بِهَا } يعني و لا تكتمها عليا (عليه السلام) و أعلمه بما أكرمته به
narrations.chain: from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Its interpretation is: do not proclaim aloud the wilaya of Ali and the honor I have given him until I command you; and 'do not murmur it' means do not conceal it from Ali, but inform him of the honor I have given him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قال رجل عنده الله أكبر فقال الله أكبر من أيّ شيء فقال من كلّ شيءٍ فقال عليه السلام حدّدته فقال الرجل كيف أقول قال قل الله أكبر من أن يوصف

text.en: A man said in his presence, 'God is greater.' He asked: greater than what? The man said: than everything. He said: you have limited Him. The man asked: how should I say it? He said: say, God is greater than to be described.

perspectives.en: On the command 'Be neither loud in your prayer, nor murmur it', the traditions read the verse differently. The Imams take it as a standing measure for reciting the ritual prayer: al-Sadiq directs a middle recitation and says a prayer-leader should recite moderately so those behind him can hear [19]. Ibn Kathir instead frames it as a Meccan occasion: the Prophet would raise his voice, the polytheists would curse the Quran, so he kept a middle course, and after the migration to Medina this lapsed and he could do as he wished [35].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: والآية من غرر الآيات القرآنية تنير حقيقة ما يراه القرآن الكريم من توحيد الذات وتوحيد العبادة قبال ما يراه الوثنية من توحيد الذات وتشريك العبادة.

sources.gloss: This verse is among the Quran's most radiant, illuminating its doctrine of oneness of essence and oneness of worship, against the idolaters who hold oneness of essence yet scatter worship.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: واختلف في هذه الآيات التسع فقيل هي يد موسى وعصاه ولسانه والبحر والطوفان والجراد والقمل والضفادع والدم عن ابن عباس والضحاك

sources.gloss: The commentators differed over these nine signs; it is said they are Moses's hand, his staff, his tongue, the sea, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وأنزلناه متفرقاً لم ننزله جميعاً إذ كان بين أوله وآخره نيف وعشرين سنة

sources.gloss: We sent it down in separate parts, not all at once, for between its beginning and its end were some twenty-odd years.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ورويت هذه القراءة عن أمير المؤمنين (ع)

sources.gloss: This reading, with 'I certainly know', is related from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him).

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: لان مشركي قومه لما سمعوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يدعو الله تارة بأنه الله وتارة بأنه الرحمن، فظنوا أنه يدعو إِلهين

sources.gloss: because when the polytheists of his people heard the Prophet call upon God sometimes as 'Allah' and sometimes as 'al-Rahman', they supposed he was calling upon two gods.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قلت: العصا، و إخراجه يده من جيبه بيضاء، و الجراد، و القمل، و الضفادع، و الدم، و رفع الطور، و المن و السلوى آية واحدة، و فلق البحر. قالوا: صدقت

sources.gloss: I said: the staff, his bringing his hand white from his bosom, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the raising of the Mount, manna and quails as one sign, and the splitting of the sea. They said: you have spoken truly.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يضع ذقنه على الأرض، إن الله عز و جل يقول: { يَخِرُّونَ لِلأَذْقَانِ سُجَّداً }

sources.gloss: He places his chin on the ground, for God, Mighty and Majestic, says, 'they fall down on their faces in prostration.'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ليقرأ قراءة وسطا، يقول الله تبارك و تعالى: { وَلاَ تَجْهَرْ بِصَلاَتِكَ وَلاَ تُخَافِتْ بِهَا }

sources.gloss: Let him recite in a middle voice; God, blessed and exalted, says, 'Be neither loud in your prayer, nor murmur it.'

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: قل الله أكبر من أن يوصف

sources.gloss: Say: God is greater than to be described.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: كان إذا صلى بأصحابه، رفع صوته بالقرآن، فلما سمع ذلك المشركون، سبوا القرآن … فلما هاجر إلى المدينة، سقط ذلك، يفعل أي ذلك شاء

sources.gloss: When he prayed with his companions he would raise his voice with the Quran, and when the polytheists heard it they cursed the Quran … and when he migrated to Medina this lapsed, and he could do whichever he wished.
